key_risks.why_it_matters: A current ratio of 0.14 means the company has only 14 paise in current assets for every rupee of current liabilities, creating a high risk of default on short-term obligations.
EBITDA margins have fallen from 7.01% to 5.42% over two years, suggesting that revenue growth is not translating into proportional profitability, possibly due to cost pressures or pricing issues.
Debt-to-equity has nearly tripled from 0.29 to 0.96, indicating the company is taking on significant debt, which increases financial risk especially given the low margins and liquidity.
The IPO is only 0.35x subscribed on the first day, signaling investor skepticism about the valuation or business quality, which could lead to a poor listing performance.
